text:
PyTorch 2.5.1 requires cuBLAS workspace configuration for deterministic CUDA matrix multiplications with CUDA ≥10.2. Before CUDA initialization, read `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`: preserve exactly `:4096:8` or `:16:8`; set `:4096:8` if absent; reject or explicitly correct any other value before initialization. `setdefault` alone leaves invalid existing values untouched. If initialization already occurred with an invalid configuration, restart the process. NVIDIA documents a possible performance penalty for `:16:8` and approximately 24 MiB additional GPU memory for `:4096:8`. Reproducibility guarantees depend on toolkit version and GPU architecture/SM count. [PyTorch 2.5.1 reproducibility](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/v2.5.1/docs/source/notes/randomness.rst), [CUDA 12.1 cuBLAS](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.1.0/cublas/index.html#results-reproducibility).

Recommended application preflight, rather than a documentation-mandated recipe: save deterministic-enabled/warn-only state, cuDNN benchmark/deterministic flags, float32 matmul precision and affected TF32/reduction flags. Enable `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=False)`, disable cuDNN benchmarking, and use explicit precision settings. Run a small nontrivial CUDA GEMM plus the actual scoring path twice on identical fixed inputs in evaluation/inference mode; synchronize, require finite scores and exact same-shape equality. Restore settings, model mode and any consumed RNG state in `finally`. Invalid configuration, CUDA/cuBLAS exceptions, nonfinite scores or same-shape repeatability failure block deterministic measurements; an environment check alone cannot establish readiness.

Test batch-shape sensitivity separately: compare singleton and batched scores using declared tolerances, maximum absolute/relative errors and ranking changes. PyTorch explicitly allows floating-point differences between batched and sliced computations because arithmetic order can differ. Such differences do not establish nondeterminism; near ties can still change recommendations, so keep measurement batching fixed. [PyTorch 2.5.1 numerical accuracy](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/v2.5.1/docs/source/notes/numerical_accuracy.rst).
